cases.title: returns the exact default config and offline result without configured TSAs
cases.positive: Actual loadTimeConfig on a fresh mode0700 workspace without.amc gives the literal default config.
cases.decisive: Actual timestampDigest returns exactly that config, grant:null, failures:[]; no fixture listener is started.
cases.limit: Public return/early-return behavior only, not universal no-I/O proof.

cases.title: skips an unmatched anchor before the wire beside a matching-anchor refusal
cases.positive: A matching genuine supplied anchor reaches the owned listener and produces named HTTP500 refusal first.
cases.decisive: Missing-anchor route has zero requests before later result assertions; matched-next route is actually reached and the two named failures remain ordered.
cases.limit: Configured anchor selection only, not signed trust-list verification.

cases.title: preserves literal attempt and failure order through finite HTTP, malformed and imprint refusals
cases.positive: Independently verify existing public token with original signed digest/fixed nonce/root; a single-TSA HTTP500 wire control then passes.
cases.decisive: Literal single-positive/http-first/malformed-second/genuine-third request order precedes null-grant and exact named HTTP500/TST_MALFORMED/TST_IMPRINT_MISMATCH failure-order assertions.
cases.limit: The other digest is a fixed literal proven different from the fixture digest; no random nonce inequality, forged AttestedTime or successful fallback grant.

cases.title: continues after the unchanged 10000 ms default abort to a real next-route refusal
cases.positive: Literal TSA_TIMEOUT_MS10000; no timeoutMs property is supplied. First route withholds every response byte and closes only after the actual client abort.
cases.decisive: The next finite HTTP500 route is actually reached; actual measured duration/failure strings/routes are logged before assertions.
cases.limit: Public requestTimestamp exposes failure message strings, not typed client AbortError code; candidate expects Node22 message The operation was aborted. No shortened timer, fake clock, delay assertion or deadline override.

resourceContract: One new owned mode0700 temp workspace per body. Network bodies bind one exact127.0.0.1 ephemeral HTTP listener; the offline body creates no listening handle.

Normal checkScopedEgress and all guards remain active. No initWorkspace, malformed workspace, active-policy/registry, vault, key, ledger, native fixture, DNS override, env mutation or imported fixture helper.

Request/response/socket errors and terminal promises are installed at acquisition. Only actual ECONNRESET/EPIPE on the explicitly stalled allowPeerAbort request are categorized as expected peer aborts.

Stop accepting with ordinary server.close, await natural request/response/socket terminals, remove only the owned temp root and emit safe finite lifecycle facts. No socket.destroy, closeAllConnections, timer/retry, signal or global cleanup.
A sole body failure is thrown unchanged. Actual additional cleanup failures form a primary-first AggregateError; repeated identical owned error objects are not duplicated.

futureControlWitnesses.first: Literal wire order, after single-element finite refusal positive.
futureControlWitnesses.masks: Earlier genuine-token or wire-positive/setup failure masks this; later result/code/body assertions may be masked by the order failure.

futureControlWitnesses.first: Literal actual second/third dispatch sequence after first caught HTTP500 or real default abort.
futureControlWitnesses.masks: Later grant/failure-string assertions are masked if dispatch assertion fails; lifecycle and timeout facts remain emitted.

futureControlWitnesses.first: Zero requests for the missing-anchor route after the actual matching-anchor wire positive.
futureControlWitnesses.masks: Later route/result/failure assertions receive no credit after the first zero-wire failure.
